entities.name: PMID:27506393
observations: Retrospective chart review of 297 adults and 2,216 esophageal dilation sessions; 93% had benign strictures.
Among bougie sessions, major adverse events were 0.5% with rule-of-3 non-adherence versus 1.6% with adherence (P=.18); perforation was 0% versus 0.7% (P=.18).
Malignant strictures, not rule-of-3 violation, predicted major adverse events and perforation; study was underpowered for rare events.

entities.name: PMID:31141071
observations: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data in 12 adults with simple benign strictures treated with progressive Savary dilation to 15 mm in one session, violating the rule of 3.
No serious adverse events were reported; absence of a comparator and very small sample limit inference.

entities.name: Rule-of-3 evidence
observations: Available adult evidence does not demonstrate that non-adherence increases perforation or other major adverse-event risk in selected benign-stricture practice.
The rule of 3 lacks a validated trial-based threshold and is best characterized as expert consensus or practice convention.
Evidence cannot establish equivalence or safety for malignant strictures, high-risk anatomy, severe or complex strictures, or uncontrolled large increments.
